hard_rules: No resume bullet points anywhere in this file. Bullets are written by the downstream generator, not stored here.

summaries.one_line: Software engineer and published researcher whose work spans embedded firmware, distributed data systems and applied machine learning; incoming MS in Computer Science at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.
summaries.short: Software engineer at Qualcomm India (January 2023 - July 2026) on the Device Firmware Update team, with prior software engineering internships at Intel Solutions & Services India and Epsilon. Three peer-reviewed publications across computational biology, causal inference and document AI. B.E. in Computer Science from RV College of Engineering (GPA 9.22); incoming MS CS at UIUC, August 2026.
summaries.long: Abhay Harish Kashyap is a software engineer whose experience covers three distinct layers of the stack. At Qualcomm India he worked on the Device Firmware Update team from January 2023 to July 2026, joining as an Associate Engineer and being promoted to Software Engineer, where he owned SoC upgrade solutions, a data-relay mechanism, a core DFU refactor delivered across two major client releases, and the upgrade framework used to deploy embedded ML models to hearable devices. At Intel Solutions & Services India he worked in Customer Engineering on EV-telemetry JSON processing, cryptographic acceleration for a national stock exchange, and a Spark/Kubernetes/Kafka ETL pipeline. At Epsilon he benchmarked and optimized HBase, Apache Phoenix and Solr for large-scale retrieval. In parallel he led and published research: biomarker prediction for non-small cell lung cancer (Cancer Informatics), conditional independence testing on HPCC Systems with LexisNexis (JAIT), and deep-learning business-document recognition and table extraction (ICAIC 2025). He also led a Samsung Research Institute Bengaluru collaboration on instant-app technology that won an Excellence Award, and co-built retrieval-augmented educational tooling now used by over 1,000 teachers across 270+ schools in southern Karnataka.

projects.situation: Predict the involvement of specific genes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Input was patient-derived transcriptomic data that had already undergone differential gene expression and pathway analyses; the goal was to apply machine learning to extract insights into NSCLC-associated biomarkers.
constraints: The dataset was heavily skewed toward genes unrelated to NSCLC pathways
Genomics was outside his primary field, requiring self-study of genome sequencing and biochemical pathways
Four candidate models were producing only mediocre precision late in the project

actions.action: Proposed analyzing the dataset to determine which features actually influence a gene's role in NSCLC pathways, rather than using all available features as the team initially assumed.
Analyzed and tested multiple under-sampling and over-sampling algorithms to address the class skew.
Selected the NearMiss method to under-sample the data, correcting the skew and avoiding a biased model.
Standardized the features before modelling.
Evaluated multiple machine learning and ensemble algorithms on the gene expression analysis data.
Used ROC curve analysis to narrow the four candidate models down to the Random Forest classifier.
Optimized the Random Forest classifier to identify critical genes linked to NSCLC.
Handled data cleaning, key-parameter identification and interpretation accuracy for the ML portion.
Produced presentations with visual aids so the wider team could follow the complex portions of the work, and contributed written sections to the research paper.
